decisions.executionNote: Raise and turn the right gripper toward a top grasp, approaching the basket in the right workspace with small continuous increments.
Continue overhead approach to the rear-right egg, increasing downward wrist tilt while keeping elbow-up continuity.
Align the right gripper vertically over the rear-right egg and descend toward grasp height; checking clearance from adjacent eggs.
Lower around the rear-right egg, then close the gripper while holding pose. Grasp retention will be judged after lifting.
Lift the closed gripper clear of the basket and begin transfer toward the holder; watch whether the egg follows.
Carry the visibly retained egg toward the rear-right holder cup, tilting inward while keeping the right EE on its own side.
Lower the retained egg over the rear-right cup and correct its leftward alignment before releasing.
An egg is visible in the rear-left cup; open and withdraw upward from the lid area, then orient toward the next basket egg.
Replan after the rejected withdrawal using a much smaller initial motion, opening first and easing upward away from contact.
Use a tiny continuity-restoring adjustment while opening, then withdraw gradually upward and right.
Approach the remaining rear-left basket egg from above with the open right gripper; the first egg remains visible in its cup.
Finish vertical alignment and descend carefully around the rear basket egg; keep the jaws open until centered.
Make a small centering correction, lower to the egg sides, and close. Basket clearance and grasp retention remain uncertain until the lift.
Hold the observed pose while closing, then make a short vertical test lift to check whether the rear egg follows.
The egg did not follow the test lift. Reopen and correct forward/right while descending for a better centered grasp.
Back off the basket rim and rotate the open jaws to approach the egg from a less obstructed direction.
Replan from the observed wrist pose: move inward from the basket edge, then descend with the rotated open jaws.
Descend a further three centimeters around the centered rear egg and close the jaws, maintaining the rotated approach.
Lift the closed gripper clear of the basket and gradually reorient for transfer; verify that this egg remains between the jaws.
Transfer the retained second egg over the empty rear-right cup, finishing the inward tilt and beginning a controlled descent.
Seat the second egg in the rear-right cup with a short descent, then open the gripper without lateral motion.
Two eggs are visible in the holder. Withdraw upward and right with open jaws, turning back toward a basket grasp.
Align over the front-left basket egg, rotating the open jaws away from the neighboring egg before descending.
Descend with open jaws around the front-left egg, using the near-vertical wrist and small centering corrections.
Center slightly left around the third egg, close the jaws, and begin a short test lift.
Lift the visibly retained third egg clear of the basket and rotate toward the empty rear-right holder cup.
Bring the third egg over the empty rear-right cup, correcting farther back than the previous placement while maintaining a closed grasp.
Lower the third egg directly into the empty rear-right cup, retaining the grasp until its seating alignment can be checked.
Three eggs are visible in the holder. Open and withdraw from the lid and cups, then turn toward the last basket egg.
Replan after the tracking interruption. Narrow the empty jaws and retreat slowly to the right, clearing the partially lowered lid before rising.
Approach the last basket egg from above with open jaws, keeping clear of the holder and gradually rotating the wrist.
Finish the near-vertical alignment and descend around the final egg with open jaws, leaving room for a final visual centering check.
Lower the open jaws to the final egg's sides, close after a small centering correction, and begin a short retention test.
Lift the final egg from the basket and tilt inward for the remaining front-left cup, keeping the grasp closed.
Carry the final egg over the remaining front-left cup, keeping the right wrist on its own side and the egg above the occupied cups.
Shift the retained egg left over the last empty cup before lowering, avoiding the egg already in the front-right cup.
Lower the fourth egg toward the front-left cup with a small rightward correction, retaining the grasp until it is close to the holder bottom.
Center the fourth egg slightly right, release it over the last cup, and begin a small upward withdrawal without pressing farther down.
Withdraw the open gripper upward and right to inspect whether the fourth egg has settled inside the front-left cup.
All four eggs are visible in cups. Close the empty jaws and move above and behind the open lid to prepare a forward-and-down closing sweep.
The lid is partly lowered. Bring the closed fingertips forward and down over its top to finish closing without contacting the eggs directly.
The lid appears fully closed. Withdraw clear of the holder and begin returning both arms to their original poses with continuous elbow-up motion.
Continue the unobstructed return toward the right home position, gradually leveling the wrist while the closed holder remains undisturbed.
Complete the gradual return to the original arm poses, with both grippers open and clear of the closed holder.
Make the final small home-pose correction and hold still while the closed holder settles.
